title: Introduce context-wash-runner and utilization-slab-reporter
author: Dana Ruiz
release_notes: Add a new synthetic runner (context-wash-runner) that simulates interleaved short/long contexts and a utilization-slab-reporter that summarizes per-kernel occupancy and KV-cache wash effects. No API or config breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: We need a compact runner that reproduces a realistic 'context wash' pattern where short conversational turns and occasional long-context generations interleave, causing repeated KV-cache churn and transient occupancy spikes. Existing runners skew either short-chat or long-stream workloads; this PR introduces a hybrid runner and a new reporting pipeline to attribute utilization to short/long phases and to detect KV-cache washouts.

What this PR does: 1) Adds context-wash-runner: a configurable workload generator that emits sessions with probabilistic context-length transitions, controlled priming ratios, and temperature-aware prefetch injection. 2) Adds utilization-slab-reporter: aggregates per-GPU/kerneltag occupancy into slab bins (0-25%, 25-50%, 50-75%, 75-100%) and correlates slabs with KV-cache miss bursts. 3) Integrates a lightweight CSV+JSON exporter for downstream visualization and an optional compact flame snapshot writer for hotpath inspection. 4) Adds unit + integration tests and documentation in docs/bench/context-wash.md.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc in ENG-1723 - [x] Runner implementation + CLI flags (--short-prob, --long-mean, --prefetch-temp) - [x] Reporter implementation + retention knobs - [x] Tests: deterministic seed cases and end-to-end smoke - [x] Perf test harness integration and example workloads - [x] Docs and README updates

Commits (high level): - init: add runner scaffolding and workload model - implement: context transition state machine + prefetch hooks - add: utilization-slab-reporter and slab aggregator - add: CSV/JSON exporter and flame snapshot writer - tests: add deterministic replay tests and CI integration - docs: usage examples and tuning guidance - ci: add new job bench/context-wash to TeamCity config

Changed areas/files (summary): - bench/context_wash/runner.py: new runner with state machine and sampling utilities - bench/context_wash/model.py: workload model and serializers - bench/reporters/util_slab_reporter.py: aggregation logic and exporters - bench/reporters/flame_snapshot.py: compact flame exporter - tests/bench/test_context_wash.py: unit+integration tests - docs/bench/context-wash.md: usage and tuning - ci/teamcity/bench.yml: add bench/context-wash job - packaging/setup.py: include new modules - examples/context-wash/example.yaml: example workload spec

Test and CI: Initial CI run failed lint on variable naming; fixed in second commit. Integration bench job ran on heterogeneous small cluster; collected slab histograms and CSV artifacts. Lightweight smoke tests assert stability and deterministic outputs for seed=42. All CI checks are green on merge.

Review summary: - Oliver Chen: requested clearer separation between occupancy slabs and utilization percent (addressed by renaming internal fields and added doc comments). - Priya Kaur: asked for reproducible seeds and deterministic CSV headers; added tests and fixed header ordering. - Marcus Bell: suggested adding a knob to disable flame snapshots in small runs (added --flame=false). There were minor nits on doc wording that were addressed.

Performance notes and findings: Sample run on a 4xA100 testbed with mixed short/long traffic (short mean 12 tokens, long mean 2048 tokens) showed transient occupancy spikes to 86% driven by long-context priming; KV-cache miss bursts aligned with short->long transitions creating measurable p95 latency increases (~18%). Utilization-slab-reporter successfully flagged slab occupancy shifts and produced per-kernel histograms that point to attention and kv-lookup kernels as hot contributors. This data will feed ENG-2045 for scheduling policy experiments.

Merge: Squash merge performed after approvals. Merged by Dana Ruiz.

Notes for maintainers: - The runner is intentionally lightweight; it avoids heavy tokenization to keep repeatability across testbeds. - Default config uses conservative prefetch temp (0.7) to limit noise; ramp up in dedicated experiments. - If you see noisy slab drift on small clusters, disable flame snapshots or increase sampling_interval.
